title: 1964 AHSME Problem 26
statement: In a ten-mile race First beats Second by \(2\) miles and First beats Third by \(4\) miles. If the runners maintain constant speeds throughout the race, by how many miles does Second beat Third?

solutions.text:
Relative to First’s speed, Second’s speed is \(\frac{8}{10}=\frac{4}{5}\) and Third’s is \(\frac{6}{10}=\frac{3}{5}.\) Thus Third runs \(\frac{3}{4}\) as fast as Second. When Second finishes \(10\) miles, Third has run \(10(\frac{3}{4})=7\dfrac12\) miles, so Second wins by \(2\dfrac12\) miles.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: When First finishes, Second and Third have run \(8\) and \(6\) miles
Compare Third’s distance when Second completes \(10\) miles
